openings.claim: Separate clearance setting from retention: a card spacer establishes lateral stop clearance during assembly, while straps retain the hatch against separation through independent attachments. Neither function is deleted; the spacer no longer lies in the strap tension path.
openings.delta: Candidate: drill/cut only the aluminum strips into two removable padded rim-clamp assemblies whose projecting edges locate the hatch. Use a supplied 1 mm card sequentially to establish stop clearances, then remove it. Attach the two fabric straps across the 180 mm direction to the clamps; tether removable parts with cord. Comparator: the same clamps and straps, with the clearance card placed beneath one strap contact during closure, coupling spacer placement to retention pressure. Do not restore this coupling in the candidate.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: clamp friction and strap tension alone explain stability; spacer-path separation adds nothing. Candidate predicts less opposite-corner lift than the coupled comparator at comparable strap tension, while meeting position, pull, reopening and seal requirements. Equal lift or worse displacement defeats the proposed benefit; inconsistent hand tension leaves interpretation uncertain.
openings.probe: First verify accessible rim undersides, clamp grip, strap reach and stop placement outside the seal footprint without altering hatch or trough. If feasible, conduct two comparator closure/pull trials, one centered and one with the required right-rim card. Then conduct ten candidate opening/closure/pull cycles, disturbing the final closure. Record ruler displacement and corner lift, 20 N pull response, stopwatch reopening time and visible seal tears. Candidate passes only all specified outcomes after ten cycles. Comparator supplies a limited contrast, not ten-cycle durability evidence.
assumptions: Rim cross-section, hatch thickness and attachment clearance are unspecified; supplied strips, six bolts and four pads must form stable removable clamps and lateral stops.
Both 250 mm straps must reach secure attachments across the hatch without powered assistance.
Comparable manual tension is not instrumented; two comparator trials cannot establish reliable causal performance.
Fabrication must fit ninety minutes and observations twenty minutes; poor grip, obstructed opening, seal damage or unavailable geometry defeats this candidate without relaxing constraints.

assessment: A bounded link-break probe, not a deployed joint. Geometric feasibility and informative tension matching remain unproven; twelve trials allocate ten-cycle evidence only to the candidate.
